item.title: When seconds matter: Why in-building coverage is a lifeline for school safety
item.description: During a school emergency, every minute that passes is crucial, but in those moments, a reliable connection can mean the difference between confusion and coordinated response.

item.title: AI in edtech: The 2026 efficacy imperative
item.description: AI has crossed a threshold. In 2026, it is no longer a pilot category or a differentiator you add on. It is part of the operating fabric of education, embedded in how learning experiences are created, how learners practice, how educators respond, and how outcomes are measured. That reality changes the product design standard.

item.title: The death of the static textbook: Why financial education must be “live”
item.description: Imagine trying to teach a student how to navigate the city of New York in 2026 using a map from 1950. The streets have changed names, new bridges have been built, and the traffic patterns have completely changed and are unrecognizable.

item.title: Despite platform fatigue, educators use AI to bridge resource gaps
item.description: Sixty-five percent of educators use AI to bridge resource gaps, even as platform fatigue and a lack of system integration threaten productivity, according to Jotform's EdTech Trends 2026 report.

item.title: The digital divide redux: Why AI is the new broadband
item.description: Remember the early 2000s, back when high-speed internet felt like a luxury reserved for the tech elite and the lucky few with deep pockets? We called it the Broadband Gap or Equity of Access, and it influenced who got ahead and who got left behind.

item.title: School Specialty Expands Learning Beyond the Screen with New Outdoor Furniture Line
item.description: Childcraft expands early learning beyond four walls and screens with durable, sustainable furniture designed for outdoor discovery.

item.title: How early cognitive training leads to lifelong brain strength
item.description: As we continue to make strides in understanding the brain--its strengths and weaknesses, how it develops, and its incredible potential--one idea has continued to strike conversation: the profound benefits of cognitive training.

item.title: New research challenges fears about AI in the classroom
item.description: Rather than replacing student thinking, when teachers design and guide AI experiences, the technology is most often used to deepen critical thinking and strengthen instruction

item.title: Mis-identifying “504-only” students
item.description: Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, which prohibits discrimination against students and other individuals with disabilities, is far less visible than the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) in school districts.
